rationale: Recurs four times on this page as the spatial-cosmological term for the manifest world-system, paired with 'the elements' and 'the Church' as parallel registers. Possibly Greek χάος or a Lycopolitan reflex of ⲕⲁϩ; functions as 'cosmos.' Distinct from ⲡⲧⲏⲣϥ ('the All') and ⲡⲕⲁⲍ ('the land').

Lycopolitan substantival form of ⲛⲁϭ 'great' with epenthetic ϩ (cf. ⲛⲉϩⲁⲓⲱⲛ same dialect feature). Takes masc/fem articles. Functions as a divine title: 'the Great One of the Spirit' at the topmost cosmic register, paralleling ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ̄ 'the Greatness.'

Lycopolitan ⲧⲁⲍⲙ = Sah. ⲧⲱϩⲙ 'call, summon, invite' + ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'out, forth.' Used here of emanation: the gods/angels are 'summoned forth from him' — emanative-vocative semantics, the divine call producing manifestation.

proposed_english: stand firm in him / grow established in him
rationale: ⲣⲍⲱⲧ likely from ⲣⲱⲧ 'grow, sprout, be established firmly' with reflexive prefix. Idiomatic 'be planted/rooted firmly in.' Used of cosmic stability of beings within their source. Cf. ⲉⲧⲥⲙⲁⲛⲧ ⲛⲍⲏⲧϩ (line 20) as semantic parallel.
Lycopolitan ⲱⲁⲣⲡ = ϣⲟⲣⲡ̄ 'first.' ⲡⲱⲁⲣⲡ ⲛⲣⲱⲙⲉ = the First Man (Manichaean Primal Man / Ohrmazd-bay), father of the Five Light Sons. Standard Manichaean cosmogonic figure.

Lycopolitan †ⲟⲩ = 'five' (= Sah. ϯⲟⲩ); ⲱⲏⲣⲉ = ϣⲏⲣⲉ 'son.' The Five Sons of the Living Spirit (= the five architects of the cosmos) and Five Sons of First Man (= the five light elements: aether, wind, light, water, fire) are foundational Manichaean entities.
ⲡⲣⲱⲙⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉⲗⲓⲟⲥ in Manichaean ecclesiology — title of the Pillar of Glory and/or the elect-perfected. ⲭⲏⲕ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ = 'completed, perfected' qualitative.

Standard Manichaean title for the Light-sent missionary figure (Mani himself in his ecclesiological function, and by extension each of the apostolic forerunners). Parallels 'Pillar of Glory' as the Eudaimonia-figure at the church register.
Greek loanword ἀρχηγός — 'leader, founder, chief.' Restored here in pairing with ⲛⲥⲁⲍ 'teachers'; together the ecclesiastical hierarchy of the holy Church.
